name: @projexlight/sdk-mcp-bridge
summary: Two-way MCP (Model Context Protocol) bridge for ProjexCloud: register external MCP servers a tenant wants to expose to their AI agents (e.g. their Salesforce MCP, their internal-tools MCP), and conversely expose this tenant's own SDK surface as MCP tools to AI clients. Foundation for any AI-agent surface; sdk-semantic's capability graph (G9) routes intents through here.

endpoints.description: Bridge health: count of registered servers + their last-seen reachability.
Register an external MCP server (URL, auth, capability tags).
Fetch a single registration + its tool list.
Disable a registration without deleting it (e.g. while debugging).

events.name: mcp-bridge.server.registered.v1
events.description: External MCP server registered; carries url + capability tags.

events.name: mcp-bridge.tool.invoked.v1
events.description: Tool call dispatched through the bridge; carries server, tool, persona, duration, ok.

events.name: mcp-bridge.exposed-server.requested.v1
events.description: External AI client opened a session against this tenant's exposed MCP surface.

models.description: Per-registration row: url, auth_ref (sdk-secrets ref), capability_tags, enabled.
Cached tool list per registration: name, description, input_schema_json.
Per-call audit row: server, tool, persona, duration_ms, ok, error_class.
Per-exposed-surface row: name, scope (which SDKs to expose), auth profile.

hooks.name: registerExternalServer
hooks.description: Add an external MCP server. Credentials wrap via sdk-secrets; capabilities discover at registration + cache.

hooks.name: invokeTool
hooks.description: Dispatch a tool call to a registered external server. Audited + rate-limited per (tenant, server).

hooks.name: exposeOwnSurface
hooks.description: Expose this tenant's SDK surface as an MCP server (used by sdk-semantic for cross-domain bridging).

hooks.name: discoverCapabilities
hooks.description: Re-fetch a registered server's tool list. Background worker runs daily.

scenarios.title: Tenant registers their existing Salesforce MCP server
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer already runs a Salesforce MCP for their internal AI bots; they want ProjexCloud agents to use it too without redeploying.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Registration row written; bridge fetches tool list + caches. Emits .server.registered.v1. ProjexCloud AI agents can now call those tools through invokeTool.

scenarios.title: AI agent calls a tool on the registered server
scenarios.when_to_use: Cloud-builder agent decides it needs to call 'salesforce_create_lead'. The bridge routes the call to the right registered server + audits the invocation.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tool call dispatched; result returned. Emits .tool.invoked.v1 with duration + ok. Rate-limited per (tenant, server).

scenarios.title: Expose this tenant's SDK surface as a tenant-owned MCP server
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer wants to integrate ProjexCloud into Claude Code / Cursor for their devs. exposeOwnSurface boots an MCP endpoint per their auth profile.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns mcp_url; customer pastes it into their AI tool's mcp.json. Each call hits a tenant-scoped MCP endpoint that authorizes via sdk-rebac before dispatching.

scenarios.title: Reactive: re-validate registrations after secret rotation
scenarios.when_to_use: secrets.secret.rotated.v1 fires; any MCP registration whose auth points at the rotated secret needs a connectivity re-test before depending on the new credentials.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Each affected registration re-tested. Failed ones disabled + ops paged with the failure context.

scenarios.title: Daily capability re-discovery catches upstream tool drift
scenarios.when_to_use: External MCP server adds / removes tools; bridge's daily discovery refreshes the cached tool list so AI agents don't try to call removed tools.
scenarios.expected_outcome: tool table refreshed; removed tools tombstoned. Subsequent invokeTool calls for removed tools fail fast with a structured error.

compliance_posture.notes: External MCP servers are third-party processors — registration captures the URL + auth scope for the CC6.7 vendor inventory. Tool invocation audit chain is the EU AI Act decision-trace lever for any AI-agent decision that touched an external tool. Credentials always vault-wrapped via sdk-secrets.
